title: Test Case Handling Check
description: Predict which edge-case categories a given set of flags exercises.

questions.prompt: How does HackerRank typically grade a submission?

options.text: Pass/fail as a single whole
Per test case, awarding partial credit
Only on code style
By comparing runtime against other submitters

questions.explanation: Grading is per test case — a submission can pass some hidden cases and fail others, earning partial credit.

questions.prompt: Why do hidden test cases often target inputs like zero or a single element?

options.text: To slow down the judge on purpose
Because general-case logic quietly breaks on these boundary inputs
Because they're easier to write than normal cases
They're only used in certification tests, never regular problems

questions.explanation: Boundary inputs like zero, negative, empty, or single-element frequently expose assumptions baked into general-case code.

questions.prompt: Why can a truthy check like `if (value)` silently break on a numeric edge case?

options.text: Because `0` is falsy, so a valid zero value gets treated as absent
Because truthy checks always throw on numbers
Because negative numbers are always truthy
Truthy checks never cause issues with numbers

questions.explanation: `0` is falsy in JavaScript, so code guarding on truthiness can wrongly treat a legitimate zero as missing data.

questions.prompt: Given the input line `neg empty zero`, sorted alphabetically, what should be printed?

options.text: neg empty zero
empty neg zero
zero neg empty
none

questions.explanation: Alphabetical order of {empty, neg, zero} is empty, neg, zero — regardless of the order tokens arrived in.

questions.prompt: If none of the four known flags (`empty`, `zero`, `neg`, `single`) appear in the input, what should be printed?

options.text: An empty line
none
all
An error

questions.explanation: The literal word `none` is the defined output when no recognized edge-case category is present.
